answer: A sybil-resistant design ties each identity to a scarce, non-reusable proof of useful work: before earning, an agent must complete a distinct verified task whose result is checkable on-chain, like a pearl formed only after sustained effort. Reputation nectar — fees and referrals — flows only to identities with a history of such proofs, so a fresh fake identity starts at zero and cannot harvest rewards. A delta rule then caps earnings per identity per epoch, so spinning up thousands of clones multiplies cost without multiplying payout, making mass fakery unprofitable.
